questions.question: You approach an intersection with a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection, even when you have a green light. Protect pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as the traffic around you.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and match the speed of the traffic. Always yield to other vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: T intersection.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: Can you drive on public or private property to avoid a traffic signal?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if the property owner gives permission.
Yes, if you are running late.
Yes, if a police officer tells you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a police officer tells you to.
questions.explanation: Driving on public or private property to avoid a traffic signal is illegal. The only exception is when a police officer directs you to do so.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
You cannot see as well at night.
Crashes happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it hard to see. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles cannot be seen from 500 feet away.

questions.question: What happens if you break the rules of a Graduated Driver License?

options.text: Nothing serious happens.
You only get points against your license.
No negative consequences happen.
You may get a fine and your license suspended.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may get a fine and your license suspended.
questions.explanation: First-time drivers with a Graduated Driver License must follow strict rules. Breaking these rules may result in a $100 fine and suspension of your license.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Driver mistakes
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Driver mistakes
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking an over-the-counter drug and driving?

options.text: Read the labels on the drug.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway, no matter what the label says.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about driving. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about taking medication and driving.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk behind your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always look behind your car before backing up. Check through the back window and your mirrors. When children are nearby, get out and check behind the vehicle before backing.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You do not have to stop.
You should slow down to check if traffic is clear.
You should stop where you can see 200 feet in both directions, even if you enter the intersection.
You should stop where you can clearly see traffic coming before entering the intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should stop where you can clearly see traffic coming before entering the intersecting road.
questions.explanation: When there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest spot to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver holds their left arm and hand pointing downward, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a car using this hand signal.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in residential districts is:

options.text: 10 mph.
25 mph.
45 mph.
65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in residential districts is 25 mph. Follow posted signs if a different speed limit is shown.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, you can pass from the lane that has the broken line.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you can proceed. However, watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. Slow down enough to stop if the light changes before you enter.

questions.question: You should turn on your headlights:

options.text: One half hour after sunset.
One half hour after sunrise.
When parked at a school.
When stopped at a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: One half hour after sunset.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when windshield wipers are on due to rain or snow, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to retaliate.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm around aggressive drivers. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures. Put as much distance between your car and theirs as possible.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: At a red light, you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: You may continue carefully through an intersection when the light turns yellow if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light changes to yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light changes to yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, continue through carefully.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you finish the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something other road users do not expect. Signal when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed. This helps drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and traffic crossing.
Slow down without stopping.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and traffic crossing.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and check for pedestrians and other traffic. Wait for the intersection to clear before moving.

questions.question: The Implied Consent Law:

options.text: Allows someone else to drive your vehicle.
Requires drivers to wear seat belts.
Means drivers agree to a breath test if arrested for drinking and driving.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means drivers agree to a breath test if arrested for drinking and driving.
questions.explanation: By driving on New Jersey roads, you agree to take a breath test if you are arrested for drinking and driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and be careful.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden under the seat.
Stops the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should feel comfortable with about a fist's width between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. You must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, pull to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the right lane. You should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely, then put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the right lane to turn, continue to the next intersection and make your turn from the correct lane.
